punchline: In one study of graduates, reaching goals of growth and community went with better health, while reaching money and fame did not.
thirty_sec: Researchers at Rochester had recent graduates rate how much they cared about money, fame and image versus growth, relationships and community. People tended to reach what they cared about, but only the growth and community goals went with better psychological health. Reaching the money goals did not, and was linked to signs of ill-being. The study is correlational, based on self-reports, and Daniel Pink uses its framing to argue for purpose over profit.
